findings.surface: S3 request authentication / anonymous principal (too strict)
findings.claim: With --auth on (the default), every unsigned request is refused 403 AccessDenied before any handler runs. A public-read bucket policy (Principal "*"), a public-read ACL, Public Access Block (IgnorePublicAcls / RestrictPublicBuckets), Requester Pays and the website endpoint are therefore never evaluated, so AWS's anonymous 200 for public objects is unreachable.
findings.root_cause: MultiServiceRouter::authenticate asks authenticator_for for an authenticator that recognizes the request. SigV4Authenticator::recognizes claims only an Authorization header starting 'AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 ' or a query X-Amz-Algorithm of that value; an unsigned request matches none, so authenticator_for returns the framework ACCESS_DENIED before dispatch. S3's own anonymous-aware authorization (state::request_is_anonymous, request_authorization::denial, Bucket::requester_pays_anonymous_refusal) only runs inside operation handlers and is never reached. The S3 service then words the refusal from the request presentation as AccessDenied 'Access Denied'.
evidence: GitHub issue #438 (unsigned GetObject 403 with IsPublic:true policy; AWS control curl to noaa-goes16.s3.amazonaws.com returned 200; v1.0.385)
GitHub issue #353 (unsigned HeadBucket 403 with no x-amz-bucket-region)

findings.claim: Correctly signed, unexpired SDK presigned S3 GET/PUT/HEAD URLs are refused 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch at the current head, and legacy SigV2 query-credential URLs (AWSAccessKeyId/Signature/Expires) are refused 403 outright because no authenticator recognizes them.
findings.root_cause: The query-signed canonical request/string-to-sign rebuilt by SigV4Authenticator (signable_uri_with_signed_host strips the six X-Amz-* fields, signable_path decodes and re-encodes the S3 path, payload() chooses UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD) does not reproduce the SDK's signature; the in-repo replay attributes the refusal to that canonical-request mismatch. Any framework Unauthenticated denial of a request carrying an issued key is then re-worded by S3 as SignatureDoesNotMatch with signing diagnostics, so the actual failure reason is hidden. The legacy three-field form matches no authenticator (recognizes only reads X-Amz-Algorithm) and no HMAC-SHA1 verifier exists.
evidence: GitHub issue #51 (presigned GET/PUT from Java 2.27 S3Presigner and JS SDK v3; 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch on browser headers)

findings.claim: Every S3 request carrying a cross-site Origin (any value, including the emulator's own origin) or Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site/same-site is refused before authentication with the invented message 'Requests a browser sends from another site are refused', regardless of the bucket's CORS rules; actual GET/PUT/HEAD/DELETE/POST responses never carry Access-Control-Allow-Origin, Expose-Headers or Vary. CORS response headers are emitted only by cors_preflight::allowed (exhaustive rg: no other access-control-* emission exists in the S3 crate), i.e. only for OPTIONS, and OPTIONS is answered via override_routing_error before the guard runs.

findings.surface: Error contract for authentication refusals (too strict / wrong code)
findings.claim: S3 re-words EVERY framework Unauthenticated denial from the request's own SigV4 presentation, ignoring the framework's actual code and message. Consequently a browser-Origin refusal is reported as 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch under --auth on, and as 403 AccessDenied 'Requests a browser sends from another site are refused' under --auth off; invalid session tokens, expired keys, malformed presign fields and wrong credential-scope services likewise collapse into SignatureDoesNotMatch whenever the key id resolves to an issued credential.
findings.root_cause: EmulatedService::refusal_response intercepts ProtocolError::Unauthenticated and calls authentication_refusal_response, which takes sigv4::presented() and calls refusal_for. refusal_for derives the answer only from X-Amz-Expires / X-Amz-Date / credential presence / issued(key id); with an issued key and no other condition it unconditionally returns SignatureDoesNotMatch with canonical-request diagnostics. With --auth off, SigV4Authenticator::minted_credentials() is None so issued() is false, refusal_for returns None and the framework's own (invented) AccessDenied sentence survives. This is the exact mechanism of #51's two-column table.
evidence: GitHub issue #51 (table: Origin + default auth -> 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch; Origin + --auth off -> 403 AccessDenied 'Requests a browser sends from another site are refused'; broken-signature control gets the same answer)
findings.verified: verified (code-derived mechanism reproduces both columns of the #51 table; #51 is a recorded run at v1.0.322)
findings.fixability: fixable in services/: pass the framework's Denied code/message through refusal_response instead of re-deriving, and reserve sigv4::refusal_for for genuine signature/expiry/skew refusals
findings.aws_reference: Amazon S3 API Reference 'Error responses' (AccessDenied, SignatureDoesNotMatch, RequestTimeTooSkewed, AuthorizationQueryParametersError are distinct codes with distinct bodies); AWS returns no message resembling 'Requests a browser sends from another site are refused'

findings.claim: The credential scope's region is never validated against the bucket/endpoint region. A request signed with any region (e.g. us-west-2) is accepted by a bucket in ap-northeast-1; AWS refuses 400 AuthorizationHeaderMalformed with a <Region> element and the fixed message naming both regions. No AuthorizationHeaderMalformed refusal exists anywhere in the workspace.
findings.root_cause: SigV4Authenticator::verify checks only scope[3] (signing name, via signed_for_serving) and the aws4_request terminator; scope[1] (date) and scope[2] (region) are ignored as validation inputs. with_signing_params feeds region straight back into the re-signing, so any region the client signed with is self-consistent and verifies. Test 'signed in another region' explicitly asserts Ok(()). S3's request_region merely echoes the scope region into aws:RequestedRegion.

findings.claim: An aws-chunked PutObject with STREAMING-UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD-TRAILER is accepted without verifying the trailer checksum against the decoded payload, without checking the trailer header name against x-amz-trailer, and the server recomputes (rather than verifies) the reported ChecksumCRC32. A wrong CRC32 and a mismatched trailer name both answer 200 and store the object; AWS answers 400 BadDigest / 400 MalformedTrailerError and stores nothing.
findings.root_cause: aws_chunked::decode breaks on the zero-length chunk and deliberately discards everything after it ('trailers ... skipped, not verified'); decode_request then rewrites content-length and removes the framing headers before the operation runs. chunked_upload::trailer_checksum_algorithm only maps x-amz-trailer to an algorithm name, and state::stored_object_checksum computes a digest over the stored bytes. The auth layer verifies chunk signatures only for STREAMING-AWS4-HMAC-SHA256-PAYLOAD markers and stops at the zero chunk, so trailer records are never parsed. Missing x-amz-decoded-content-length is handled separately (411) by chunked_upload::RefuseUnframedChunkedBody.

findings.surface: Object key '/' routing (too strict / destructive; adjacent to the auth lens)
findings.claim: Object operations on the key '/' (and keys made only of slashes) execute the same-method BUCKET operation: DeleteObject deletes the bucket, PutObject runs CreateBucket and stores nothing, HeadObject runs HeadBucket, GetObject returns a ListBucketResult as the object body.

findings.surface: Virtual-hosted-style endpoint / TLS front door (too strict)
findings.claim: An HTTPS request to <bucket>.<announced-endpoint-authority> aborts the TLS handshake (SSLV3_ALERT_ILLEGAL_PARAMETER), so presigned URLs and SDK requests using S3's default addressing form never receive any S3 answer; the SigV4 scope/skew refusals those checks exercise are unreachable.
findings.root_cause: The data port's rustls config is built from TlsCertificateAuthority::covering(Some(client_host)) — a certificate naming only the announced loopback/bind host; a bucket-prefixed authority is not covered. The router does contain path_style_for_virtual_hosted rewriting for requests that do complete the handshake, but the front door rejects the host first.
evidence: issues/things-that-do-not-work/20261029T083133Z-s3-virtual-hosted-style-bucket-addressing-is-unreachable.md (virtual-hosted addressing silently degrades to path style)
findings.verified: verified by in-repo replay (three check ids) at the cited commit; code is consistent, emulator not re-run at HEAD
findings.fixability: requires core TLS/listener change (wildcard SAN / SNI handling) plus host-based bucket resolution
findings.aws_reference: Amazon S3 virtual-hosted-style addressing (<bucket>.s3.<region>.amazonaws.com) is the SDK default; recorded AWS 400 AuthorizationHeaderMalformed for the cross-region PUT in the same check

findings.surface: SigV4 signing-name scope (too lenient; unverified AWS side)
findings.claim: A request whose credential scope names any S3-family signing name (s3, s3express, s3-outposts, s3-object-lambda) is accepted by a service serving another S3-family name; the workspace's own test asserts an s3express-signed call served by the s3 service is Ok(()).
findings.root_cause: verify() uses signed_for_serving, which returns true whenever both the scope service and the serving signing name match signs_like_s3(); no comparison with the endpoint's actual signing name is made. The comment states 'Any S3-family name serves any other'.
evidence: exhaustive search of claims.jsonl / in-repo S3 docs: no recorded AWS response refusing a cross-signed S3-family request
findings.verified: unverified on the AWS side (emulator behaviour is code- and test-verified; no AWS recording in the corpus)
findings.fixability: fixable in core/: compare the scope's signing name against the serving service's own signing name, with an explicit allowlist only where AWS really shares one
findings.aws_reference: UNVERIFIED — AWS SigV4 credential scope's service field is expected to name the endpoint's signing name; no measurement in this corpus

findings.surface: Presigned/query parameter validation (too lenient; unverified AWS side)
findings.claim: Malformed and boundary X-Amz-Expires values are not answered as AWS's 400 AuthorizationQueryParametersError: a non-numeric value falls through to SignatureDoesNotMatch (expires_out_of_range returns None and Signature::of fails to parse), and '0' is explicitly accepted by the range test. A junk x-amz-decoded-content-length on an aws-chunked body is ignored rather than refused, and an arbitrary x-amz-content-sha256 value containing '-' is trusted as a precomputed marker.
findings.root_cause: sigv4.rs::expires_out_of_range treats only negative and numeric-over-ceiling values as out of range; its own test asserts 'not-a-number' -> None and '0' -> None. request_authentication.rs::Signature::of returns None on a non-numeric Expires, and S3 re-words that denial as SignatureDoesNotMatch (F-04). aws_chunked::decode_request parses x-amz-decoded-content-length with parse().ok() and treats a failure as 'no declared length'; chunked_upload::remember counts any non-empty value as present, so no 411 either. payload() treats any hyphenated x-amz-content-sha256 as SignableBody::Precomputed without validating the marker set.
evidence: issues/things-that-now-work/20261027T093123Z-s3-2-net-new-root-causes-in-sigv4.md:22-26 (recorded AWS 400 AuthorizationQueryParametersError + fixed message for X-Amz-Expires=604801 only)
findings.verified: unverified on the AWS side: only the over-ceiling case (604801) has a recorded AWS refusal; no recording found for non-numeric Expires, Expires=0, junk decoded-content-length or arbitrary hyphenated payload markers. Emulator behaviour is code- and unit-test-verified
findings.fixability: fixable in services/ and the shared decoder after AWS behaviour is measured; the S3 refusal schema already carries AuthorizationQueryParametersError/400
findings.aws_reference: UNVERIFIED — Amazon S3 API Reference 'Authenticating requests: using query parameters'; only the 604801 case is recorded in this corpus

coverage: LENS=s3-auth. Ground-truth sources: /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-research-2026-11-19/census.json (572 GitHub issues with bodies+comments, 5355 open in-repo docs, 17671 fixed-doc index, 7114 stubs), claims.jsonl (13041 rows: 572 gh_issue + 5355 inrepo_open + 7114 stub), census.md, linkedin-post.txt, the 5355 markdown docs under /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-2026-11-19/aws0/issues/things-that-do-not-work/, the 17671 fixed docs under things-that-now-work/, and the code under services/, vendor/, core/. All JSON was queried with python3 -I (streamed line-by-line for claims.jsonl; never dumped into context); literal scans used rg over the whole workspace. I read all seven assigned GitHub issues in full with bodies and comments (#51, #26, #438, #353, #421, #565, #500), and enumerated all 46 GH issues whose title/family touches auth/CORS/presign/S3 (including #180, #72, #316, #566). Of the 5355 open docs, keyword sweeps found 271 mentioning SigV4/signature fields, 111 presign, 89 CORS/cross-origin, 96 anonymous/unsigned and only 1 aws-chunked/framing; 168 S3-relevant docs matched the combined lens regex and were indexed; 46 are labelled family=s3. I read ~18 of those docs in full plus ~10 fixed docs (73 fixed docs match the lens by title/filename). I read the four assigned source files in full or in large part (services/.../service/sigv4.rs 1151 lines, request_authorization.rs 1480 lines, cors_preflight.rs 610 lines, vendor/server/src/request_authentication.rs 654 lines), plus vendor/smithy-server-runtime/src/multi_service_router.rs, vendor/server/src/listener_guard.rs, vendor/server/src/listeners.rs, vendor/server/src/lib.rs, vendor/smithy-schema-server/src/aws_chunked.rs, vendor/smithy-schema-server/src/rest_xml.rs, services/.../chunked_upload.rs, service.rs, state.rs, ops/create_bucket.rs, ops/head_bucket.rs, post_object.rs, wire.rs, the S3 crate's own tests, and aws-sigv4 1.6.5 from Cargo.lock. Both divergence directions are covered: too-strict (F-01,02,03,04,05,09,10,11,16,17) and too-lenient (F-06,07,08,12,13,14,15,18,19). 'affected_claims' counts the distinct corpus claim rows (distinct GitHub issue numbers + distinct in-repo doc filenames) cited in each finding's evidence; code file:line citations and trace ids are not counted. Parity is NOT claimed: several divergences are deliberately marked unverified or partially verified, and no check from linkedin-post.txt is asserted to pass.
gaps: The emulator was never built or run: no replay suite, no live AWS call, no curl. Every behavioural statement is either a recorded corpus observation (GitHub issue / in-repo replay doc) or a code-reading conclusion; findings verified='unverified'/'partially verified' say so explicitly.

GitHub issues describe released binaries at other commits (e.g. #565 v1.0.523 / 864dd26a, #51 and #26 v1.0.322 / 7753983c, #438 v1.0.385, #353 v1.0.338, #421 v1.0.353, #500 v1.0.471), while the audited tree is fork_head ec5f6fbab9238221b966379f06846c34e9d6a6f5 with a single squashed commit. Release behaviour and HEAD source can differ; #26's preflight 501 and the >100-CORS-rules wording are examples already fixed at HEAD and are NOT reported as current divergences.

In-repo open docs are snapshots taken at their own Issue-Commit values and the docs themselves warn 'the code base you are currently working in can have drifted'; fixed docs under things-that-now-work/ are historical, not proof of current behaviour. I checked each reused cause against current code where feasible.

The exact root cause of the presigned SigV4 signature mismatch (F-02) is not proven: the replay doc attributes it to the canonical request/string-to-sign rebuilt for a query-signed request, but the S3 refusal re-wording (F-04) can produce the same 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch from an unrelated framework denial. I did not bisect or instrument the verifier.

linkedin-post.txt check #1 ('a presigned S3 PUT with a different content-type -> 403') is underspecified: the emulator does feed every name in X-Amz-SignedHeaders into the recomputed signature (vendor/server/src/request_authentication.rs:154-158), so a changed signed content-type would be refused, but no corpus replay measures that exact case. Check #2 ('no valid SigV4 -> denied') is satisfied by the emulator for the wrong reason: it denies ALL unsigned requests, including public ones AWS serves (F-01). No check is declared passing.

AWS-side behaviour is NOT measured for F-13 (Access-Control-Allow-Credentials), F-14 (Allow-Headers from rule vs echo, 32-header cap), F-16 (#500 says 'We haven't run this against AWS'), F-18 (cross-signed S3-family scopes) and F-19 (non-numeric/zero Expires, junk decoded-content-length, arbitrary hyphenated payload markers). These are marked unverified; do not treat them as confirmed AWS divergences.

Not exhaustively audited: all 5355 open docs and 17671 fixed docs were indexed/searched but not individually read; the 7114 stub files were only counted; other services' auth paths (Cognito, CloudFront, Lambda function URLs) were sampled only to establish that refuse_cross_site_browsers is global.

Not covered by this lens: IAM policy-evaluation fidelity beyond the anonymous front door, SSE-KMS, bucket-policy condition keys, CloudFront OAC/OAI, and the 32 MiB PutObject 413 ceiling, although several appear in the same multi-cause docs.
No claim of parity achieved; the LinkedIn post's framing ('5 checks real AWS rejects') was not validated end-to-end against real AWS in this audit.
